cases.name: row
cases.when: layout is "table" -- the wide layout, where the row is a <tr> inside ArenaTable's grid
cases.reason: Every requirement that applies to a row in this shape is a clause of the `grid` pattern ArenaTable binds: the row role, the roving tab stop across the cells, and the Enter that activates the row all live on the <table> and are recorded there. The row role is not written here at all -- the element supplies it -- and the row owns none of the rest, which is why binding an interactive pattern here would claim a route this element does not have: the same reason ArenaTab binds `none` under `tabs` and ArenaSideNavItem binds `none` under `navigation`. A <tr> also cannot become a <button>: a button may not be a child of <tbody>, and the row's actions cell draws the consumer's real buttons inside it.

cases.name: card-interactive
cases.when: layout is "card" and `interactive` is true -- below --bp-md the row is still a <tr>, and role="button" replaces the row role the element carries natively

cases.name: card-inert
cases.when: layout is "card" and `interactive` is false -- the default, and nothing obliges a consumer to change it
cases.reason: With `interactive` false there is nothing to press, so no interactive pattern applies. The card is a <tr> with no tab stop and no activation, and it declares role="presentation" so the row role the element carries natively does not describe a stack of cards as a table. This is the shape that keeps a dead tab stop off every row of every table that is not clickable.
